name: Heather pink
lede: Heather pink is a vivid, slightly purplish pink standardized by RAL in 1927, named for the fresh flowers of the heather shrub rather than its faded, grey-toned Heather grey sibling.

sections.title: A flower's own pink
sections.body:
RAL 1927 is the source given for Heather pink here, with the hex value an approximate screen rendering of the printed standard [1]. Heather's small bell-shaped flowers bloom in exactly this register, a magenta-leaning pink across moorland in late summer; the color library groups it under "heather" as a family word, the brighter counterpart to the greyed Heather grey [2]. The ISCC-NBS system would file it as a deep purplish pink [2]. In Munsell terms it sits near 5.0RP 5.4/12.0: high chroma, near the boundary of red and purple [2].

The nearest named color is [[france-rose|France Rose]], 4.4 units away and duller; [[rose-color|Rose Color]] sits at 4.9, more vivid [2]. The library also lists Heather Violet as a close alternate name [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our 23,781-painting archive carries a match for Heather pink, as photographed [3]. That describes the archive, not painting as a whole: this saturated a pink, at this exact hue, rarely survives in old oils once varnish and age have had their effect [3]. Its paler, greyer sibling Heather grey, by contrast, turns up in dozens of paintings here, which is itself a small lesson in how fugitive a bright pink pigment can be next to a muted one [3].
